historical_references.reference: Sammu, also known as Sammakeshara, was a powerful king of the Satavahana dynasty who ruled around 110 CE. He is noted for his patronage of Buddhism and extensive building activities, including the construction of the rock-cut Buddhist caves at Nagarjuni Hill in Maharashtra.
historical_references.context: Satavahana Dynasty, Patronage of Buddhism, Construction of Rock-cut Buddhist Caves

historical_references.reference: Sammu is also the name of a king who ruled over the northern part of the Vakataka Empire in the late 4th and early 5th centuries CE. He is known for his military campaigns against the Gupta Empire and the Huna invasion, as well as his patronage of art and architecture, including the construction of the rock-cut temples at Ajanta and Ellora.
historical_references.context: Vakataka Empire, Military Campaigns Against Gupta Empire and Huna Invasion, Patronage of Art and Architecture
